subject: Architecture
title: Water Waste in Buildings
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Water Waste in Buildings.

hook.text: A typical office building wastes 30% of the water it uses. Most of it goes straight down the drain.

buildup.text: Toilets, cooling towers, and irrigation consume vast amounts of treated drinking water unnecessarily.

discovery.text: Rainwater harvesting and greywater recycling can cut a building's water consumption in half.

twist.text: Singapore's Marina Bay Sands collects rainwater from its rooftop pool deck to supply its cooling systems.

climax.text: The Living Building Challenge requires buildings to generate all their own water — a radical standard.

punchline.text: We flush toilets with drinking water. Architecture can fix that.

quiz.question: How much water does a typical office building waste?
